places.name: Wynwood

places.name: Overtown

periods.label: 1900s
periods.summary: Plena takes shape in Ponce, Puerto Rico, around the turn of the century. Miami, incorporated in 1896, is a young railway town at the end of Henry Flagler's Florida East Coast line.

periods.label: 1910s
periods.summary: Overtown's Lyric Theater opens in 1913 and Miami Beach is incorporated as its own city in 1915. The Jones–Shafroth Act of 1917 makes Puerto Ricans US citizens, the legal basis for later migration to the mainland.

periods.label: 1920s
periods.summary: Florida's land boom drives rapid building in Miami and Miami Beach until the 1926 hurricane. Under segregation, Overtown grows into a busy centre of Black business and entertainment.

periods.label: 1930s
periods.summary: Most of Miami Beach's Art Deco hotels and apartment buildings go up in this decade, giving South Beach its pastel, streamlined look. Overtown's nightlife thrives.

periods.label: 1940s
periods.summary: After the Second World War, Puerto Ricans begin moving to New York in large numbers, and in 1948 the Empire Windrush brings Caribbean migrants to Britain. In Miami, Overtown's clubs host touring Black stars who are barred from staying in segregated Miami Beach.

periods.label: 1950s
periods.summary: Sound systems take hold in Kingston, and Claudia Jones founds the West Indian Gazette in London in 1958 and stages a Caribbean carnival there in 1959. The Cuban Revolution of 1959 begins the exile that remakes Miami's Little Havana.

periods.label: 1960s
periods.summary: Fania Records is founded in New York in 1964, and the first Notting Hill street carnival is held in 1966. In Miami, interstate construction cuts through Overtown and displaces much of its historic community.

periods.label: 1970s
periods.summary: On 11 August 1973, DJ Kool Herc's party at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue in the Bronx becomes hip hop's most widely cited starting point, and the Nuyorican Poets Café begins the same year. The Miami Design Preservation League forms in 1976, and the Miami Beach Architectural District is listed on the National Register in 1979.

periods.label: 1980s
periods.summary: The 1980 Mariel boatlift brings about 125,000 Cubans to South Florida. Miami bass takes off in the middle of the decade as hip hop spreads from New York to London and beyond.

periods.label: 1990s
periods.summary: Reggaeton takes shape in San Juan's underground, mixing hip hop with Jamaican dancehall and Spanish-language reggae. South Beach's preserved Art Deco district becomes the backdrop to its revival.

periods.label: 2000s
periods.summary: Grime emerges in East London, Art Basel holds its first Miami Beach edition in December 2002, and reggaeton reaches a worldwide audience. Wynwood Walls opens in Miami in 2009.

periods.label: 2010s
periods.summary: Wynwood becomes an international street-art destination, and the Black Cultural Archives open on Brixton's Windrush Square in 2014. Hurricane Maria devastates Puerto Rico in 2017, the same year Puerto Rican artists top charts worldwide with 'Despacito'.

periods.label: 2020s
periods.summary: Hip hop marks fifty years in 2023, counted from the Sedgwick Avenue party, and the Windrush generation marks seventy-five years since the ship's arrival. Monumental Streams opens in this decade, with Miami as its gateway.

movements.name: Bomba
movements.summary: One of Puerto Rico's oldest living traditions, an Afro-Puerto Rican music and dance with roots traced to the 17th century among enslaved Africans on the island's coastal plantations. Dancers and lead drummers hold a conversation: the dancer's moves call, the drum answers. Loíza remains one of its strongest centres.

facts.label: Instruments
facts.value: Barriles (barrel drums), maracas and the cuá (sticks played on wood)

movements.name: Plena
movements.summary: A Puerto Rican song form that took shape in Ponce around 1900, carried on hand-held frame drums called panderos. Its verses told the news of the day, earning it the name 'el periódico cantado', the sung newspaper.

movements.name: La Gran Migración
movements.summary: After the Second World War, hundreds of thousands of Puerto Ricans, US citizens since 1917, moved to the mainland, most of them to New York City. Cheap flights from San Juan made it one of the first large migrations by air. They built communities in East Harlem, the Lower East Side and the Bronx that shaped the city's music, politics and language.

movements.name: New York salsa
movements.summary: Built in New York by Puerto Rican and Cuban musicians from Cuban son and mambo, with Puerto Rican rhythms woven in. Fania Records, founded in 1964 by Johnny Pacheco and Jerry Masucci, became the sound's best-known label.

facts.label: Fania Records
facts.value: Founded in New York in 1964 by Johnny Pacheco and Jerry Masucci

movements.name: Nuyorican movement
movements.summary: From the late 1960s, poets, playwrights and artists of Puerto Rican descent in New York claimed the word 'Nuyorican' and wrote in English, Spanish and the mix between them. The Nuyorican Poets Café, begun in 1973 on the Lower East Side, became the movement's home.

facts.label: Nuyorican Poets Café
facts.value: Begun in 1973 by poets including Miguel Algarín, Miguel Piñero and Pedro Pietri; now at 236 East 3rd Street

facts.label: Anthology
facts.value: 'Nuyorican Poetry', edited by Miguel Algarín and Miguel Piñero, published 1975

movements.name: Sound-system culture
movements.summary: In 1950s Kingston, operators such as Duke Reid and Clement 'Coxsone' Dodd built mobile sound systems — towering speakers, a selector and a deejay talking over the records — that turned yards and street corners into dances. The practice fed ska, reggae and dub, and travelled with Jamaican migrants to London and New York.

movements.name: Hip hop's origins
movements.summary: Hip hop grew out of block parties and community-centre dances in the Bronx in the 1970s. DJ Kool Herc, who had moved from Kingston, extended the drum breaks of funk records on two turntables, and MCs, b-boys and b-girls and graffiti writers built a culture around them. By 1979, the Sugarhill Gang's 'Rapper's Delight' had carried rap onto the charts.

facts.label: 11 August 1973
facts.value: Back-to-school party thrown by Cindy Campbell, with her brother DJ Kool Herc on the decks, at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue
facts.source: Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture

facts.value: The Sugarhill Gang release 'Rapper's Delight', rap's first US Top 40 hit

movements.name: Windrush generation
movements.summary: The name given to people who came to Britain from Caribbean countries between 1948 and 1971, after the HMT Empire Windrush brought passengers from Jamaica and other islands to Tilbury in June 1948. They and their children helped rebuild post-war Britain and changed its music, food and language.

facts.label: June 1948
facts.value: The Empire Windrush docks at Tilbury, Essex, with passengers from the Caribbean
The Immigration Act 1971 marks the commonly used end date of the Windrush generation

movements.name: Notting Hill Carnival
movements.summary: A street carnival first held in Notting Hill in 1966 and now staged every August bank holiday weekend, with steel bands, masquerade costume bands and static sound systems. Its roots include the indoor Caribbean carnival that Claudia Jones organised at St Pancras Town Hall in January 1959, after the Notting Hill race riots of 1958.

facts.value: Caribbean carnival organised by Claudia Jones at St Pancras Town Hall
First outdoor event, a neighbourhood fayre widely credited to community worker Rhaune Laslett

movements.name: Lovers rock
movements.summary: A romantic, soul-inflected style of reggae made in South London from the mid-1970s, often sung by young Black British women and played at house parties and sound-system dances. Louisa Mark's 'Caught You in a Lie' (1975) is widely cited as an early landmark.

movements.name: Grime
movements.summary: A fast, hard-edged London sound of around 140 beats per minute that emerged in East London in the early 2000s, spread through pirate radio, raves and clashes. Bow produced two of its defining artists, Wiley and Dizzee Rascal, and Tottenham crews brought Skepta and JME.

facts.value: Dizzee Rascal wins the Mercury Prize for 'Boy in da Corner'

movements.name: Reggaeton
movements.summary: Grew out of San Juan's 1990s underground, where DJs and MCs mixed hip hop with Jamaican dancehall and Spanish-language reggae from Panama on cassette mixtapes. Daddy Yankee's 'Gasolina' (2004) carried it to a worldwide audience.

facts.value: Daddy Yankee releases 'Gasolina', an international breakthrough for the genre

movements.name: Miami Beach Art Deco
movements.summary: Between the early 1920s and the early 1940s, and above all in the 1930s, hundreds of small hotels and apartment buildings went up in South Beach in a tropical take on Art Deco and Streamline Moderne. Pastel colours, porthole windows, 'eyebrow' sunshades and nautical motifs became the look of Miami Beach.

movements.name: Miami Design Preservation League
movements.summary: Founded in 1976 by Barbara Capitman, Leonard Horowitz and fellow campaigners to save South Beach's Art Deco buildings from demolition. Their campaign won National Register listing for the Miami Beach Architectural District in 1979.

facts.label: Listed
facts.value: Miami Beach Architectural District added to the National Register of Historic Places, 1979
facts.source: US National Register of Historic Places

movements.name: Overtown's golden era
movements.summary: From the 1920s to the 1950s, Overtown's theatres, clubs and hotels made it a centre of Black entertainment in the segregated South, nicknamed the 'Harlem of the South'. Touring Black stars who played Miami Beach but were barred from staying there often lodged and performed after hours in Overtown. Interstate construction in the 1960s broke the neighbourhood apart.

movements.name: Cuban exile in Miami
movements.summary: After the Cuban Revolution of 1959, successive waves of Cubans left for Miami, turning Little Havana into the centre of exile life. Their arrival reshaped the city's language, food, music, business and politics.

facts.label: Operation Pedro Pan
facts.value: 1960–1962: more than 14,000 unaccompanied Cuban children flown to the United States

facts.label: Freedom Flights
facts.value: 1965–1973: an airlift that brought hundreds of thousands of Cubans to Miami

movements.name: Mariel boatlift
movements.summary: Between April and October 1980, about 125,000 Cubans crossed from the port of Mariel to South Florida in a flotilla of boats, many sent by relatives in Miami. The arrivals, later called Marielitos, changed the city once more.

movements.name: Haitian Miami
movements.summary: From the 1970s, Haitians fleeing dictatorship and poverty settled in Miami, many arriving by boat. The community built Little Haiti, with its churches, botanicas, markets and the sound of kompa and Haitian Creole on the street.

movements.name: Miami bass
movements.summary: A Miami offshoot of hip hop from the mid-1980s, built on the booming kick drum of the Roland TR-808, fast tempos and call-and-response chants made for car stereos and parties. 2 Live Crew made it known across the United States.

movements.name: Art Basel Miami Beach
movements.summary: The American edition of the Swiss art fair, held at the Miami Beach Convention Center each December since 2002. The week of satellite fairs and events around it spreads across Miami, including Wynwood and the Design District.

facts.label: First edition
facts.value: December 2002

movements.name: Wynwood Walls
movements.summary: An outdoor mural project founded in 2009 by developer Tony Goldman, who invited graffiti and street artists to paint the walls of Wynwood's warehouses. It helped turn the district into an international destination for street art, a lineage that runs back to the graffiti writers of 1970s New York.

facts.label: Founded
facts.value: 2009, by Tony Goldman

people.name: Valid ID
people.summary: Valid ID is the inaugural presenter and featured artist introducing MONUMENTAL STREAMS. He presents WAVEMAKERS, beginning with the opening chapter 'Valid ID presents WAVEMAKERS: Puerto Rico, New York to London', and his EP 'Better Late Than Never' anchors the platform's opening artist campaign. A full biography and approved imagery will be added once they are signed off.

people.name: DJ Kool Herc
people.summary: Born Clive Campbell in Kingston, Jamaica, in 1955, he moved to the Bronx in 1967. On 11 August 1973 he played a back-to-school party organised by his sister Cindy Campbell in the recreation room at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue, an event widely cited as the birth of hip hop. Drawing on Jamaican sound-system practice, he used two copies of a record to extend the drum breaks that dancers loved.

people.name: Claudia Jones
people.summary: A Trinidad-born journalist and activist who grew up in Harlem, New York, and settled in London after being deported from the United States in 1955. In 1958 she founded the West Indian Gazette in Brixton, and in January 1959 she organised a Caribbean carnival at St Pancras Town Hall, a forerunner of the Notting Hill Carnival. She died in London in 1964.

people.name: Barbara Capitman
people.summary: A preservation campaigner who co-founded the Miami Design Preservation League in 1976 and led the fight to save South Beach's Art Deco buildings, which won National Register listing for the Miami Beach Architectural District in 1979.

people.name: Tony Goldman
people.summary: A real-estate developer (1943–2012) known for reviving historic neighbourhoods, including New York's SoHo and Miami Beach's South Beach. In 2009 he founded Wynwood Walls, inviting artists to paint the warehouses he had bought in Wynwood.

people.name: Miguel Algarín
people.summary: A poet (1941–2020) born in Santurce, San Juan, who grew up in New York. He co-founded the Nuyorican Poets Café on the Lower East Side in 1973 and, with Miguel Piñero, edited the 1975 anthology 'Nuyorican Poetry'.

routes.summary: Since the 1959 revolution, waves of Cubans have left for Miami, making Little Havana the centre of exile life.

routes.label: Mariel boatlift
routes.summary: Between April and October 1980, about 125,000 Cubans crossed from the port of Mariel to South Florida.

routes.label: From Haiti to Little Haiti
routes.summary: From the 1970s, Haitians settled in Miami and built Little Haiti into the centre of Haitian life in South Florida.

routes.label: Hip hop crosses the Atlantic
routes.summary: From the early 1980s, records, films and touring crews carried hip hop from New York to London, where it met the city's sound-system culture and fed later British forms, grime among them.

routes.label: Latin music industry exchange
routes.summary: Since the 2000s, Miami has been a major centre of the Latin music business, and many Puerto Rican artists, producers and labels work between San Juan and Miami.

routes.label: WAVEMAKERS: New York to London

videos.title: Apollo 11 launch — engines at 500 fps (camera E-8)
videos.summary: NASA's slow-motion view of Apollo 11's engines at liftoff on 16 July 1969.
videos.description:
Camera E-8 at Launch Complex 39A, Kennedy Space Center, filmed the base of Apollo 11's Saturn V at 500 frames per second as its engines ignited and it lifted off on 16 July 1969, carrying Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins toward the first crewed Moon landing. Played back at normal speed, well under a minute of flame, smoke and steam stretches to more than eight minutes.

Silent NASA engineering footage, credited to NASA/Kennedy Space Center; its use here does not imply endorsement by NASA. Launch Complex 39A is on Merritt Island in Brevard County, Florida, not in Miami. A public-domain film shown as demonstration media while original programming is produced; it is not a Monumental Original.

credits.attribution: NASA/Kennedy Space Center

videos.title: Big Buck Bunny
videos.summary: A gentle giant rabbit gets even with three woodland bullies — the Blender Foundation’s classic open movie.
videos.description:
Blender Foundation’s 2008 animated short: a big, good-natured rabbit whose peaceful morning is spoiled by three bullying rodents, until he sets about some elaborate payback. Slapstick throughout and no dialogue, so it plays for every age.

Creative Commons demonstration media, shown while original programming is produced; it is not a Monumental Original.

credits.attribution: Big Buck Bunny (c) copyright 2008 Blender Foundation | www.bigbuckbunny.org — CC BY 3.0

videos.title: Caminandes: Llama Drama
videos.summary: Koro the llama has one goal: get across the road.
videos.description:
A 90-second animated short from the Blender Foundation’s Caminandes series: Koro the llama tries, and keeps trying, to cross a road in a stylised Patagonian landscape. Wordless slapstick for every age.

Creative Commons demonstration media; not a Monumental Original.

credits.attribution: Caminandes: Llama Drama — Pablo Vazquez, Beorn Leonard, Francesco Siddi; music and sound: Jan Morgenstern (Blender Foundation) — CC BY 3.0

videos.title: Caminandes: Llamigos
videos.summary: A llama and a penguin squabble over the last berry of winter.
videos.description:
The third Caminandes short (2016): in a snowy, stylised Patagonia, Koro the llama meets Oti the penguin and the two fight over a single berry before working out that they get further together.

Creative Commons demonstration media; not a Monumental Original.

credits.attribution: Caminandes 3: Llamigos — Blender Foundation (Blender Animation Studio) — CC BY 3.0

videos.title: Coney Island at Night
videos.summary: Edison's 1905 film of Coney Island's amusement parks drawn in electric light.
videos.description:
Shot by Edwin S. Porter for the Edison company in 1905, this short film turns the camera on Coney Island after dark. Luna Park and Dreamland, both named in the film's own titles, appear as towers, domes and arches outlined entirely in electric bulbs against the night.

It is silent, with no soundtrack. A public-domain film shown as demonstration media while original programming is produced; it is not a Monumental Original.

credits.attribution: Coney Island at Night (1905). Edwin S. Porter, Edison Manufacturing Company. Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons.

videos.title: Dutch Cotton Fashion (1958)
videos.summary: A 1958 Amsterdam show of Dutch cotton designs by Cees Terleth and Dick Holthaus.
videos.description:
Dutch Polygoon newsreel from January 1958: a fashion show in Amsterdam for the Dutch cotton industry, with designs by Cees Terleth and Dick Holthaus and a glimpse of models being dressed backstage.

Creative Commons demonstration media from the Netherlands Institute for Sound & Vision; not a Monumental Original.

credits.attribution: Polygoon-Profilti (producent) / Nederlands Instituut voor Beeld en Geluid (beheerder) — CC BY-SA 3.0 NL

videos.title: Courier Satellite Launch, Florida (1960)
videos.summary: A one-minute newsreel of the Courier communications satellite lifting off from Cape Canaveral.
videos.description:
Universal Newsreel from 6 October 1960: the Courier communications satellite launches on a Thor-Ablestar rocket from Cape Canaveral, Florida — on the Atlantic coast, a few hours’ drive north of Miami.

Public-domain demonstration media; captions are machine-generated and unreviewed. Not a Monumental Original.

credits.licence: Public domain (Universal Newsreel, gifted to the public)
credits.attribution: Universal Newsreel, 6 Oct 1960 — public domain

videos.title: Amsterdam Fashion Week (1951)
videos.summary: A Polygoon newsreel of Amsterdam’s 1951 fashion week, shown outdoors in the Vondelpark.
videos.description:
Dutch Polygoon newsreel from 1 November 1951: models present the season’s suits, coats and hats outdoors in Amsterdam’s Vondelpark during the city’s fashion week.

Creative Commons demonstration media from the Netherlands Institute for Sound & Vision; not a Monumental Original.

credits.attribution: Polygoon-Profilti (producent) / Nederlands Instituut voor Beeld en Geluid (beheerder) — CC BY-SA 3.0 NL

videos.title: Fashions in Rome (1964)
videos.summary: American wool fashions modelled among Rome’s monuments, in colour.
videos.description:
Universal Newsreel from 26 October 1964, in colour: American wool fashions are modelled at the Trevi Fountain and the Roman Forum — a promotional fashion segment of its time.

Public-domain demonstration media; captions are machine-generated and unreviewed. Not a Monumental Original.

credits.licence: Public domain (Universal Newsreel, gifted to the public)
credits.attribution: Universal Newsreel, 26 Oct 1964 — public domain

videos.context: A 1964 promotional segment whose narration addresses women in dated terms (for example, dressing “to attract that certain man”).

videos.title: Kingston Jamaica
videos.summary: A 1920 educational film of Kingston's harbour, docks, streets and homes.
videos.description:
Made for the Ford Educational Library in 1920, when Jamaica was a British colony and about thirteen years after the 1907 earthquake, this silent film tours Kingston: sailing ships in the harbour, cargo on the docks, people at work and on the move, streetcars, homes, and a busy street the intertitles call Pearl Street.

It is silent, with period intertitles and no soundtrack. A public-domain film shown as demonstration media while original programming is produced; it is not a Monumental Original.

credits.attribution: Kingston Jamaica (1920). Ford Educational Library, Ford Motor Company. US National Archives, via Internet Archive.

videos.context: Made for a US company's educational film series in 1920, when Jamaica was a British colony. Its intertitles and framing reflect the colonial attitudes of the time, for example in scenes of boys diving for coins.

videos.title: Minetest — the first minutes of a new world
videos.summary: A calm screen recording of the opening minutes in Minetest (now Luanti), the open-source block-building game.
videos.description:
A 2022 gameplay recording of Minetest 5.6.1 — the free, open-source voxel game now called Luanti — showing the first minutes of a fresh world: arriving, exploring and opening the inventory. In-game sound only, no commentary.

Creative Commons (BY-SA) demonstration media, shown unaltered; not a Monumental Original.

credits.licence: CC BY-SA 3.0 (game media); recording on Wikimedia Commons
credits.attribution: Minetest gameplay recording by PantheraLeo1359531 (Wikimedia Commons); game media © The Minetest Team (Perttu Ahola et al.), CC BY-SA 3.0

videos.title: Newspaper Train
videos.summary: Len Lye's 1942 wartime film about getting London's newspapers out through the Blitz.
videos.description:
Made by the artist and filmmaker Len Lye at the Realist Film Unit for the UK Ministry of Information, this short follows the distribution of London's newspapers during the Blitz of 1940–41, through Blackfriars, Holborn, Cannon Street, London Bridge and Victoria stations and out by train to Ramsgate in Kent.

A film whose Crown copyright has expired, shown as demonstration media while original programming is produced; it is not a Monumental Original. The English captions are human-made, from Wikimedia Commons.

credits.attribution: Newspaper Train (1942). Len Lye, Realist Film Unit, for the UK Ministry of Information. Via Wikimedia Commons.

videos.context: Wartime propaganda made for the UK Ministry of Information. It includes bomb damage and an air attack on a train.

videos.title: Interior N.Y. Subway, 14th St. to 42nd St.
videos.summary: In 1905 a camera rides New York's brand-new IRT subway uptown under Manhattan.
videos.description:
On 21 May 1905, seven months after New York's first subway line opened, Biograph cameraman G. W. 'Billy' Bitzer filmed the run through the tunnel from 14th Street–Union Square to the original Grand Central station at 42nd Street. The camera follows another train through the dim tunnel and past stations, and arrives on a crowded platform. The film is in the US National Film Registry.

It is a silent actuality film with no intertitles, and this copy has no soundtrack. A public-domain film shown as demonstration media while original programming is produced; it is not a Monumental Original.

credits.attribution: Interior N.Y. Subway, 14th St. to 42nd St. (1905). American Mutoscope & Biograph Co.; camera G. W. "Billy" Bitzer. Library of Congress, via Wikimedia Commons.

videos.title: Interface Specimens
videos.summary: Studio motion concepts for the screens you use: catalogue and player, membership vault, interest cards and search.
videos.description:
Specimens from Monumental's interface studio: a neon catalogue and player, a membership vault that opens from free to premium, bright Bauhaus cards for each interest, and search with combined filters, narrowed all the way down to an empty result and back again.

Illustrative design concepts assembled as a demonstration, not programme footage; titles and counts on screen are placeholders. The Premium label on this reel shows how premium gating works; the access level is an example, not a business decision.

availability.note: Demonstration of premium gating — the access level is an example, not a business decision.

videos.title: The Living Atlas
videos.summary: Studio motion concepts for finding culture by place: a globe of light, an isometric Miami, drawn cities, a stamped passport and a discovery instrument.
videos.description:
How Monumental maps the world: a glass globe of light ringed with stories, Miami picked out neighbourhood by neighbourhood in an isometric city, Deco line drawings of cities from Miami to London, a culture passport stamped stop by stop, and the Take Me Somewhere instrument printing a ticket for a thirty-minute trip.

Everything here is illustrative concept art from Monumental's studio, assembled as a demonstration of how the platform plays, saves and connects content. It is not programme footage; the maps are not to scale, and the routes, stamps and labels on screen are design placeholders.

videos.title: Stories in Time
videos.summary: Studio motion concepts for travelling through decades, seeing why stories connect, and the title art of two planned originals.
videos.description:
A golden dial clicks through the decades and the library re-sorts by era; a thread of connections shows the reason behind every recommendation; then title art for the two planned Monumental Originals: THE STORY BEHIND THE STORY in torn paper, and WAVEMAKERS in rippling lines of light.

Illustrative concept art throughout. The decade cards are artwork, not archival footage, and the title sequences are motion design, not footage from either series, neither of which has published episodes yet.

videos.title: The Organism: Sound, Touch & Chrome
videos.summary: Studio motion concepts for the parts of Monumental that respond to you: chrome, membrane, sound, cursor and touch.
videos.description:
The Monumental wordmark in polished chrome, a tunnel of pale jointed rings that pulses like a living spine, a visual preview of the tones designed for every action, a cursor that changes shape with context, and the app built for touch.

Studio motion concepts, shown as a demonstration of the platform's sensory design rather than programme footage; the sound you hear is an ambient score, not the interface tones themselves. This reel also demonstrates an early-access window: premium members can watch it now, and it opens to everyone on 1 December 2026.

availability.note: Demonstration of an early-access window: premium members now, everyone from 1 Dec 2026. Example only — not a business decision.

videos.title: Roads to Romance: Coral Gables
videos.summary: A 1950 Chevrolet promotional film touring Coral Gables and Key Biscayne in Technicolor.
videos.description:
Made in 1950 by the Jam Handy Organization for Chevrolet, this short colour film drives a Chevrolet convertible through Coral Gables, past the new University of Miami campus and the Venetian Pool, across the Rickenbacker Causeway to Crandon Park and Cape Florida on Key Biscayne, and on to Parrot Jungle.

It is an advertisement, and it ends by sending you to your local Chevrolet dealer. A public-domain film shown as demonstration media while original programming is produced; it is not a Monumental Original. The English captions are machine-generated and have not been reviewed.

credits.attribution: Roads to Romance: Coral Gables (1950). The Jam Handy Organization for Chevrolet. Via Internet Archive.

videos.context: This is a Chevrolet advertisement: the company's cars appear throughout as product placement.

videos.title: King and Queen Leave Britain on American Tour (1939)
videos.summary: George VI and Queen Elizabeth leave London for their 1939 North American tour.
videos.description:
Universal Newsreel from 15 May 1939: King George VI and Queen Elizabeth leave Buckingham Palace and sail from Portsmouth aboard the Empress of Australia, setting out on the royal tour of Canada and the United States months before the Second World War.

Public-domain demonstration media; captions are machine-generated and unreviewed. Not a Monumental Original.

credits.licence: Public domain (Universal Newsreel, gifted to the public)
credits.attribution: Universal Newsreel, 15 May 1939 — public domain

videos.title: Democracy at Work in Rural Puerto Rico
videos.summary: A 1942 US government film on farm extension work in Puerto Rico's countryside.
videos.description:
Made by the US Department of Agriculture Extension Service and directed by Chester Lindstrom, this narrated film shows rural Puerto Rico around 1941: coffee and tobacco farms in the highlands, sugar cane on the coastal plains, extension work by the University of Puerto Rico, and 4-H clubs.

A public-domain US government film held by the National Archives, shown as demonstration media while original programming is produced; it is not a Monumental Original. No captions are available yet.

credits.attribution: Democracy at Work in Rural Puerto Rico (1942). US Department of Agriculture Extension Service; directed by Chester Lindstrom. US National Archives, via Internet Archive.

videos.context: A US government film made in wartime. It frames Puerto Rico as an 'outpost of American democracy', takes a paternalistic tone toward the people it shows, and leaves Black Puerto Ricans out of the picture.

videos.title: Senators Win World Series (1924)
videos.summary: A silent Kinograms newsreel of the Washington Senators beating the New York Giants in the 1924 World Series.
videos.description:
Kinograms’ silent newsreel of the deciding game of the 1924 World Series at Griffith Stadium in Washington, D.C. Its intertitles follow Walter Johnson pitching the last four innings to close out his first World Series, the president in the stands, and the home crowd swarming onto the field.

Public-domain demonstration media; not a Monumental Original.

credits.attribution: Senators Win World Series (Kinograms Publishing Corp., 1924). Library of Congress Motion Picture, Broadcasting & Recorded Sound Division. Public domain.

videos.title: Sintel
videos.summary: The Blender Foundation's 2010 animated fantasy about a young woman searching for a dragon.
videos.description:
A lone young woman, Sintel, crosses a harsh fantasy world in search of the baby dragon she once rescued and raised. The Blender Foundation made it in 2010 as an open movie, produced with free and open-source software.

Shown under a Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 licence as demonstration media while original programming is produced; it is not a Monumental Original. Contains fantasy violence.

credits.attribution: Sintel – © copyright Blender Foundation | www.sintel.org – CC BY 3.0

videos.title: THE STORY BEHIND THE STORY — motion teaser
videos.summary: An illustrative motion concept for the planned original series.
videos.description:
Torn-paper letters spell THE STORY BEHIND THE STORY, and four cards hang on a grey board naming what the series looks for: the decision, the relationship, the setback and the turning point.

This is an illustrative motion concept made by Monumental's studio. It is not footage from the series, which is planned and has no episodes, subjects or release dates announced yet.

videos.title: Tears of Steel
videos.summary: The Blender Foundation's 2012 live-action science-fiction short, shot in Amsterdam.
videos.description:
In a near-future Amsterdam, a group of warriors and scientists gather at the Oude Kerk to restage a crucial moment from the past, in a desperate attempt to save the world from destructive robots. The Blender Foundation made it in 2012 as an open movie, combining live action shot in Amsterdam with visual effects made in Blender.

Shown under a Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 licence as demonstration media while original programming is produced; it is not a Monumental Original. Contains mild language and science-fiction violence. The Premium label demonstrates premium gating; the access level is an example, not a business decision.

availability.note: Demonstration of premium gating with a full-length film — access level is an example, not a business decision.

credits.attribution: Tears of Steel – (CC) Blender Foundation | mango.blender.org – CC BY 3.0

videos.title: Cross-country day in the dunes (1922)
videos.summary: A 1922 Polygoon newsreel of cross-country races in the dunes near The Hague.
videos.description:
Dutch Polygoon newsreel, catalogued as “Eerste(?) veldloopdag in Nederland” — possibly the first cross-country running day in the Netherlands — organised by the Haagse Atletiek Vereniging in the dunes at The Hague, with women’s, men’s and veterans’ races.

Creative Commons demonstration media from the Netherlands Institute for Sound & Vision; not a Monumental Original.

credits.attribution: Polygoon-Profilti (producent) / Nederlands Instituut voor Beeld en Geluid (beheerder) — CC BY-SA 3.0 NL

videos.title: Valid ID presents WAVEMAKERS: Puerto Rico, New York to London
videos.summary: The opening WAVEMAKERS chapter, presented by Valid ID. In development.
videos.description:
Valid ID presents the opening chapter of WAVEMAKERS, a Monumental Original about people shaping culture across borders. The journey runs from Puerto Rico to New York to London.

This chapter is in development. Nothing has been released and no release date has been announced. When it is published, it will play here.

availability.note: In development — no release date announced.

videos.title: WAVEMAKERS — motion teaser
videos.summary: An illustrative motion concept for the opening WAVEMAKERS chapter.
videos.description:
Lines of blue light ripple like open water beneath the title card 'Valid ID presents WAVEMAKERS', and a pink thread traces the route of the opening chapter as New York, then London, light up: Puerto Rico, New York to London.

This is an illustrative motion concept made by Monumental's studio. It is not footage from the programme and contains no filmed material; the chapter itself is in development with no release date announced.

videos.title: Where the Sun Reigns
videos.summary: A mid-century booster film selling Greater Miami as a land without winter.
videos.description:
Made around 1955 by Reela Films for the Greater Miami Development Board and the Dade County Commission, this narrated promotional film sells Greater Miami to visitors and newcomers. It moves from Miami and Miami Beach across the Biscayne Bay causeways to Miami International Airport, Lincoln Road, the Miracle Mile in Coral Gables, the University of Miami, the Orange Bowl, the farms of the Redland and a Seminole attraction in the Everglades.

A public-domain film from the Prelinger Archives, shown as demonstration media while original programming is produced; it is not a Monumental Original. The English captions are machine-generated and have not been reviewed, so they contain errors.

credits.attribution: Where the Sun Reigns (c. 1955). Reela Films for the Greater Miami Development Board and Dade County Commission. Prelinger Archives, via Internet Archive.

videos.context: A mid-century tourism booster film. It presents Seminole people as an exotic attraction and shows only white visitors; the racial segregation of Jim Crow-era Miami goes unmentioned.

videos.title: West Coast Hails First World Series (1959)
videos.summary: Universal Newsreel on the first World Series played on the West Coast: Dodgers v White Sox at the Coliseum.
videos.description:
Universal Newsreel from 5 October 1959: the Los Angeles Dodgers host the Chicago White Sox at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in the first World Series games played on the West Coast. Low-resolution copy with a small glitch noted in the source catalogue.

Public-domain demonstration media; not a Monumental Original.

credits.licence: Public domain (Universal Newsreel, gifted to the public)
credits.attribution: Universal Newsreel, 5 Oct 1959 — public domain (via National Archives / Internet Archive)

videos.description:
Universal Newsreel from 2 March 1964: construction of the New York World’s Fair in Flushing Meadows, Queens, weeks before opening, followed by a Hollywood item in which the actress Hayley Mills leaves her handprints at Grauman’s Chinese Theatre.

Public-domain demonstration media; captions are machine-generated and unreviewed. Not a Monumental Original.

credits.licence: Public domain (Universal Newsreel, gifted to the public)

videos.summary: The release trailer for a free, open-source strategy game of ancient civilisations.
videos.description:
Wildfire Games’ trailer for Alpha 27 “Agni” of 0 A.D. Empires Ascendant, a free and open-source real-time strategy game about ancient civilisations. It walks through new features, maps and game modes, with stylised ancient-warfare battle scenes (no gore).

art:culture-passport.alt: A navy 'Culture Passport' with a gold compass emblem opens to a hand-drawn map with a dotted trail between Miami and San Juan, and a page of circular travel stamps, Miami and San Juan stamped and two slots still empty.

art:brand-chrome.alt: The words 'MONUMENTAL STREAMS' in polished chrome serif letters catch passing glints of light on black, mirrored below, with the line 'Explore what you love. Discover where it lives.'

art:living-membrane.alt: A biomechanical tunnel of ribbed, pearl-grey rings spirals toward a soft glowing centre, with a segmented spine running along its lilac floor.

art:sound-aurora.alt: Ribbons of aurora light drift behind a sound panel titled 'Sound: designed tones for every action', with a sound-on switch, a master level slider, output meters and six waveform tiles labelled Activate, Select, Save, Transition, Time tick and Error.

art:cursor-language.alt: A dark grid of six panels demonstrates cursor states (Explore, Play, Drag, Save, Open and Orbit), each a different small shape, above the line 'Cursor adapts to context. Native cursor remains as fallback.'

art:mobile-app.alt: Three phone screens of the Monumental Streams app on a terracotta background (a home feed, a browse view and a player) beside the heading 'Built for touch.' and the line 'Swipe, save, and resume where you left off.'

art:search-filters.alt: A pastel search screen with 'miami' typed in the search bar and filter chips for place, interest, access and duration; the results move between a grid of colourful geometric tiles and an empty state reading 'Nothing here yet. Try removing a filter.'

art:miami-isometric.alt: An isometric illustration of a Miami-area waterfront, with beach, palms, low-rise Deco buildings, glass towers, boats and a low sun, and map pins for South Beach, Wynwood, Little Havana and Brickell, under the heading 'Miami, up close.' and the note 'Illustrative map, not to scale'.

art:story-paper.alt: Cut-paper letters spell 'THE STORY BEHIND THE STORY' above four pinned paper cards with simple symbols: The Decision (a forked path), The Relationship (two overlapping circles), The Setback (a broken step) and The Turning Point (a bending arrow).

art:wavemakers-lines.alt: Flowing blue lines of light ripple like water across black beneath the title 'VALID ID PRESENTS WAVEMAKERS', with 'Puerto Rico, New York to London' along the bottom and an 'In development' tag.

art:take-me-somewhere.alt: A cream retro console labelled 'Take Me Somewhere', with a small screen listing a short itinerary, mood buttons for Chill, Lively, Culture and Late, dials for interest, time and destination, and a large red GO button.

art:placeholder.alt: Placeholder artwork: a biomechanical tunnel of ribbed, pearl-grey rings spiralling toward a soft glowing centre.

art:still-sintel.alt: Sintel, the film’s red-haired heroine, in close-up

art:organ-live.alt: A dormant beacon: a teardrop glass membrane outlined in faint signal red holds an unlit bone core inside a lantern cage of bone ribs, on a vertebral stalk, with two still red rings around it on a dark wine-violet field.

art:organ-movies.alt: An iris aperture of overlapping bone blades set in a collar of vertebrae, with warm amber light glowing through its opening, orbited by a tilted ring of filmstrip frames with sprocket holes and lit amber cells, on a dark field.

art:organ-music.alt: A vertebral spine with a harp-like bone arm strung with glowing violet strings, a tendon coiled around the spine and three rippling glass drum membranes held in bone hoops, on a deep violet field.

art:organ-sports.alt: A seamed bone ball inside a coral-rose glass membrane, circled by braided tendon arcs trailing coral light, hovering above a bowl of curved bone ribs like an arena, on a dark field.

art:organ-gaming.alt: A sphere of floating voxels, bone-white blocks with glowing cyan edges and frosted glass cubes, blooming open around a bright core, on a dark teal field.

art:organ-news.alt: A grooved bone printing drum with toothed gears on a vertebral axle, pearl paper ribbons printed with abstract lines of type curling up from it, and an antenna mast sending out pale broadcast rings, on a dark field.

art:organ-fashion.alt: A dress-form mannequin: a bone spine inside a crinoline cage of hoops and ribs, a bodice woven from glowing fibres and a sheer rose-gold drape falling from the shoulder, on a dark field.

art:organ-culture.alt: A branching growth of bone, like coral or a neuron, rising from a vertebral socket, its tips glowing verdigris and linked by thin arcs of light, on a dark green field.

art:organ-kids.alt: A chunky spiral banded in soft pastel candy colours rising from a cloud of round pebbles, surrounded by iridescent soap bubbles and twinkling sparks, on a dark violet field.
